# sandbox

An ephemeral scratch space for this session. Files you upload appear
instantly in a browser page at {{PUBLIC_URL}} so a person can check them,
and GET requests to configured upstreams ({{UPSTREAMS}}) are forwarded with
the right credentials injected, so you never need or see an API key.

Nothing here persists. /data is a RAM disk: a reset or a container restart
empties it. Copy anything worth keeping into the repository.

## Session

    curl -s {{PUBLIC_URL}}/llms.txt          # this text
    curl -s -X POST {{PUBLIC_URL}}/reset   # start clean
    ...work...
    curl -s -X POST {{PUBLIC_URL}}/reset   # leave nothing behind

Reset when the task is finished.

## Files

Paths are relative to /data. Directories are created as needed and exist
only while a file is in them. Use the layout the files will have in the
repository so they can be copied across unchanged. Percent-encode spaces
and parentheses in URLs; the path on disk is the decoded form.

    # upload (201 created, 204 replaced)
    curl -s -X PUT --data-binary @poster.jpg \
      "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/files/assets/movies/429/poster.jpg"

    # list, as text
    curl -s -H 'Accept: text/plain' {{PUBLIC_URL}}/tree

    # download
    curl -s -o out.jpg "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/files/assets/x/poster.jpg"

    # delete a file or a directory (recursive)
    curl -s -X DELETE "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/files/assets/x"

    # delete everything
    curl -s -X POST {{PUBLIC_URL}}/reset

Uploads are capped per file (default 50 MB) and the RAM disk has a fixed
size; a full disk fails the upload rather than the host.

The page at {{PUBLIC_URL}} previews images, audio, video and text (YAML,
JSON, Markdown, plain text) and updates live. Other types show a download
link. Tell the person which path to look at.

## Upstreams

Each upstream allows only the requests listed for it; anything else is
403 with the allowed list in the body. Check before guessing:

    curl -s {{PUBLIC_URL}}/upstreams      # {"tmdb": ["GET /3/movie/*", ...], ...}

    curl -s "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/tmdb/3/movie/429"
    curl -s "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/tmdb/3/search/movie?query=A%20Fistful%20of%20Dollars&year=1964"
    curl -s "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/tmdb/3/movie/429/images?include_image_language=en,null"
    curl -s -H 'Accept: application/json' "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/plex/library/sections"
    curl -s -H 'Accept: application/json' "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/plex/library/metadata/12345"

The path after /<upstream>/ is the upstream's own path and query, exactly
as its API documents them. Do not add an API key, token or Authorization
for the upstream; the server injects the credential and drops any
Authorization header you send before forwarding. Plex answers XML unless asked for JSON.

TMDb image files live on https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original<file_path>
and need no key; fetch them directly and upload the result.

## Typical Kometa flow

1. Reset.
2. Look the title up: /tmdb/3/search/movie?query=..., then
   /tmdb/3/movie/<id>/images for artwork candidates.
3. Download the artwork and upload it under the exact path it will have
   in the repository's Kometa config, e.g. assets/movies/<tmdb id>/poster.jpg
   (or background.jpg, theme.mp3). Check the repository's own
   documentation for its asset layout and size limits before uploading.
4. Upload the metadata YAML alongside, e.g. metadata/movies.yml.
5. Ask the person to check {{PUBLIC_URL}}.
6. Copy the approved files into the repository checkout, then reset.

## Routes

    GET    /                    page
    GET    /tree                HTML fragment, or text with Accept: text/plain
    GET    /preview/<path>      HTML fragment
    GET    /events              SSE, event "tree"
    GET    /files/<path>        raw file
    PUT    /files/<path>        upload
    DELETE /files/<path>        delete
    POST   /reset               empty /data
    GET    /<upstream>/<path>   proxied, subject to the allow list
    GET    /upstreams           JSON list of names
    GET    /llms.txt  /healthz  /version
